slides.headline: Does what you have already done still count?
slides.supporting: Before a career pivot, internal move, or other change in context, ask four questions.

slides.headline: Some of it does. Let’s get precise about what.
body: Your experience does not all travel.
It does not all disappear either.
The work is to tell the difference.

slides.headline: What travels?
body: Patterns you have learned to recognize.
Ways of solving problems you have already demonstrated.
These can remain useful when the employer, function, industry, or role changes.

slides.headline: What does not?
body: Assumptions that made you effective there but may mean little somewhere else.

slides.headline: What can you prove?
body: The next context cannot see your internal reputation.
It needs evidence another person can understand and trust.

slides.headline: What must you relearn?
body: A new context brings different technical requirements, language, and constraints.
Learning them takes time, even when you are capable of it.

slides.headline: Adjacent experience still has to be read.
body: Name the gap before someone else does.
Make your experience clear enough for the next context to judge the gap accurately.

headlineLines: Your experience does not all travel.
It does not all disappear either.
slides.closing: Follow for clear ways to decide your next move and prove you’re ready for it.
